result:
Brilliant. Done. Built a kitchen-sink hero detail screen per spec - back link, header with badges, four tabbed panels (Overview, Powers, Missions, Edit), schema-driven form with validation, retire confirmation dialog, and the whole thing compiles clean.

Here's what shipped:

**HeroDetailViewModel** (`hero-detail.viewmodel.ts`)
- Reads hero ID from route params, loads hero from domain service
- Manages edit form state as signals
- Validates against the zod schema, reports errors per field
- Implements save (updates hero) and retire (removes and navigates back)

**HeroDetail Component** (`hero-detail.ts`)
- Header: avatar, name/ID/alias, badges for class/status/clearance, Deploy/Retire buttons
- Manual tab interface (4 buttons, content shown via `@if (activeTab() === 'X')`)
- **Overview tab**: field summary, three mini-stat cards, right-column dossier k/v
- **Powers tab**: power index as a progress bar, class/tier badges
- **Missions tab**: deployment record showing mission count and success rate
- **Edit tab**: "Edit Hero" button that reveals schema form; form fields auto-populated; Cancel/Save buttons with loading state; separate Retire button; all form inputs properly extracted and type-converted
- Retire confirmation modal (fixed overlay) with Cancel/Retire actions

Responsive by design (grid/flex, no fixed px), uses the build spec palette and icon scheme, integrates spartan primitives throughout. The app builds with no errors — one bundle-size warning (expected with new feature).
